behaviors.behavior: QR items fold into ordinary FR-table rows, continuing the existing FR-GG.MM sequence, no new column/category marker
A spec with no QR items is unchanged: no QR rows, no stale '## Quality Requirements' heading
Regeneration whose fresh detection finds FEWER features than the run already on disk does not reuse an id an earlier run's row already meant
Regeneration does not reuse a RETIRED id either (a row under '## Removed Requirements')
sequence_of is the correct inverse of canonical_fr_id, including the FR-01.99 -> FR-02.01 group rollover
sequence_of rejects non-canonical ids (returns None, never raises)
A QR-folded FR row is readable by the FR-table reader and passes the real fr_gates existence gate under --affected-frs
The derived-catalogue summary count agrees with the rendered table when QR rows are present (trg-1aa5a8ab anti-drift invariant preserved)
A read/parse failure reading the existing spec.md refuses the write rather than silently proceeding as if no ids existed
behaviors.reason: The guard is a deliberate absence of a try/except (verified by code inspection and confirmed by spec-reviewer + code-reviewer + doubt-reviewer, none of whom found a swallowed exception path); there is no realistic way to construct an unreadable-but-present file in a portable unit test (encoding corruption behaves differently across OSes) without testing Python's own file I/O rather than this code's logic.

surface_verification.detail: CLI surface: pytest against plugins/shipwright-adopt/tests/test_spec_document.py + test_fr_id_sequence.py, the fixture directly exercising the fix (write_spec -> spec.md -> fr_table_reader round trip).
